The band right now is Quoted per linear metre on glass specification and fixing method. Quoted per linear metre. A balustrade is a structural safety element that has to resist people leaning and falling against it, so the glass specification and the fixing into the structure are the job. Where the substrate cannot carry the load, that has to be addressed first — and we will say so rather than fixing into something inadequate.

In Dainfern, with housing that is mostly estate homes, cluster and townhouse developments, the seasonal pattern is predictable enough to plan around. Booking inside the window costs less than booking in the rush, every year.

What to sort out before the season turns:

- Ask which SANS glass class is being supplied and why
- Get the glass thickness and whether it is toughened or laminated
- Ask whether removal, making good and sealing are included
- Check whether the opening is measured on site before ordering

What not to do: no drainage slots in the sill, so the frame holds water; stacking doors on a track the floor cannot keep level.

serviceName: What an Aluminium Window Actually Costs
priceBand: R350 – R800 per m² and R3,000 – R6,000 per window are both published — they describe different things
title: Need What an Aluminium Window Actually Costs in Greenside? Price band first, quote second
long:
What an Aluminium Window Actually Costs in Greenside: R350 – R800 per m² and R3,000 – R6,000 per window are both published — they describe different things.

R350 per m² and R3,000 per window cannot both be true. Here is the arithmetic..

Both figures above come from published South African cost guides gathered November 2026. Work them through on a standard 1.5 m by 1.2 m window, which is 1.8 m². At R800 per m² that is R1,440. The per-window guide says R3,000 to R6,000 for the same thing. They cannot both describe a supplied and installed window. The reconciliation is that the per-square-metre figure describes labour or supply alone, while the per-unit figure describes the finished job. Nobody in this market explains that, and it is why every buyer thinks they are being overcharged.

Why the price is published. Most trades in Gauteng quote only after a site visit, which makes comparing three quotes a week-long job. We publish the band first so you can decide whether the project is worth starting before anyone books your Saturday.

Greenside at a glance. An established suburb north-west of Rosebank, known for the Gleneagles Road restaurant strip, older character homes with wooden floors and mature gardens that bring leaf and dust into the house. Housing is mostly older freestanding houses, cottages and small complexes, around Gleneagles Road.

What a straight quote from anyone should include:

- Get the glass thickness and whether it is toughened or laminated
- Ask whether removal, making good and sealing are included
- Check whether the opening is measured on site before ordering
- Confirm the frame system name and its powder-coat warranty
- Ask which SANS glass class is being supplied and why

And what quietly inflates one: clear float glass where SANS requires safety glass; no drainage slots in the sill, so the frame holds water; a frameless shower with no hinge allowance, so the door fouls the tile.

Windows, doors and glazing quoted per square metre, fitted or supply-only

long:

long:
We get called out to the same Paving and Driveways problems over and over in Cornwall Hill. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

2. No NHBRC or council approval on work that needed it
3. Paying a deposit that buys materials nobody counted

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted per square metre on base depth, block type and area into a bigger one. Quoted per square metre with the base build-up stated in the quote. This is the single most important line in any paving price, and it is the one cheap quotes leave vague. A driveway carrying vehicles needs a far deeper base than a garden path, and paving laid on insufficient base sinks into ruts within a season or two.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Insist on a bill of quantities with the quote

How that number is derived: Pump circuits are outdoor circuits with a motor load on the end, which is why they turn up so often on failure lists. We price the circuit, the isolation and the protection as separate lines. The pump itself and the plumbing are a pool or borehole specialist's work, and for those our sister sites at sapoolpros.co.za and sawatersolutions.co.za are the right starting point.

What we are actually talking about: Pump circuits are the circuits that fail first, and the ones inspections find.

- Buying a CoC without an inspection, which is worthless at claim time
- An extension wired in without updating the CoC on record

long:
We get called out to the same Borehole Drilling problems over and over in Mooikloof. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit
2. Treating borehole water for taste and ignoring the actual lab test
3. A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper

Each one of those turns a job of R350 – R750 per metre on Gauteng drilling-company guides, with other sources claiming R700 – R1,400 into a bigger one. Four public sources gathered in November 2026 disagree by roughly double on the same job. A drilling-company city guide puts Roodepoort at R350–R650 and Centurion at R420–R750 per metre. A separate cost guide says R700–R1,200 with R950 typical. A June 2026 company announcement cites R900–R1,400. An industry body figure quoted in the press puts the average near R600. None of these is our rate card. The spread exists because sellers quote high, guides quote wide, and nobody states what is included — so ask every quote what the metre rate covers.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Confirm the stand's rated load against the full tank weight
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded

long:
If you are pricing Essential Circuit Wiring in Parkhurst, the number you want is Priced per board split — the number of circuits moved drives the cost. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: This is often the cheapest way to make a backup system work better, and it is routinely skipped. Splitting the board so backup feeds only what matters usually lets you buy a smaller inverter or generator, which saves more than the board work costs. We will show you that arithmetic before you buy equipment.

It is quoted per board, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Parkhurst specifics. A leafy northern Johannesburg suburb of older freestanding houses and cottages, with a main street of shops and restaurants. Housing here is mostly older freestanding houses, cottages and apartments, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: Deciding what stays on is a design decision, and it is where backup budgets are won.

Where quotes go wrong

- No surge protection on the main, then a R40,000 appliance claim
- Adding solar to a DB board that was already at capacity
- Buying a CoC without an inspection, which is worthless at claim time

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted per project after geotechnical and structural assessment into a bigger one. Never quoted before investigation, and be wary of anyone who does. Foundation work follows an engineer's design, and that design follows what trial holes and soil assessment actually find. The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

priceBand: Quoted per system once the water analysis is in hand
title: The expensive mistake people make with Water Filtration Systems
long:
We get called out to the same Water Filtration Systems problems over and over in Florida. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit
2. A pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house
3. A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted per system once the water analysis is in hand into a bigger one. We will not quote filtration before seeing a water analysis, and we would be suspicious of anyone who does. The correct system depends entirely on what is in the water — and on flow rate, which is the variable most often ignored until the pressure drops through an undersized filter.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration

Five things to confirm, in writing, first:

priceBand: Unit plus installation, with membrane and cartridge costs stated
title: The expensive mistake people make with Reverse Osmosis Drinking Water
long:
We get called out to the same Reverse Osmosis Drinking Water problems over and over in Florida. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit
2. A pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house
3. A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper

Each one of those turns a job of Unit plus installation, with membrane and cartridge costs stated into a bigger one. Usually the cheapest honest answer when the problem is drinking quality rather than the whole supply. Treating a few litres a day at the kitchen sink costs a fraction of treating every litre that enters the house. We state the membrane and cartridge replacement costs up front, and the waste-water ratio, because RO discards water to make clean water and nobody mentions that.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration

Why a R6,500 tank appears as R20,000 on a quote.

This is the most useful number on the site. Published retail prices put a 5,000 litre vertical tank at about R6,499 and a 10,000 litre at about R15,599, gathered from a South African source. Yet a storage tank appears on project quotes at R20,000 – R25,000. Both are real. The difference is the base, the stand, the plumbing in and out, the float or level control, the overflow and the labour. We quote the tank and the installation as separate lines so you can see which you are paying for, and so you can compare our tank price with a retailer's directly.

Why the price is published. Most trades in Gauteng quote only after a site visit, which makes comparing three quotes a week-long job. We publish the band first so you can decide whether the project is worth starting before anyone books your Saturday.

Edenvale at a glance. A well-established East Rand suburb of freestanding homes and complexes with light industry and commercial areas close to residential streets. Housing is mostly freestanding houses, townhouses and light-industrial areas, around Edenvale Hospital.

- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded

What a borehole costs per metre, and why four sources disagree by double.

Four public sources gathered in November 2026 disagree by roughly double on the same job. A drilling-company city guide puts Roodepoort at R350–R650 and Centurion at R420–R750 per metre. A separate cost guide says R700–R1,200 with R950 typical. A June 2026 company announcement cites R900–R1,400. An industry body figure quoted in the press puts the average near R600. None of these is our rate card. The spread exists because sellers quote high, guides quote wide, and nobody states what is included — so ask every quote what the metre rate covers.

Why the price is published. Most trades in Gauteng quote only after a site visit, which makes comparing three quotes a week-long job. We publish the band first so you can decide whether the project is worth starting before anyone books your Saturday.

Weltevreden Park at a glance. A Roodepoort family suburb next to the Walter Sisulu National Botanical Garden, with freestanding homes on good-sized stands, pools and gardens. Housing is mostly freestanding family homes and townhouse complexes, around Walter Sisulu National Botanical Garden.

title: Tembisa, festive shutdown, December rush and January backlog: the Double Glazing window is open
long:
It is festive shutdown, December rush and January backlog in Gauteng. That is not small talk — it changes both the price and the queue for Double Glazing.

The band right now is Large, custom or double glazed units run R7,000 – R15,000+ per window on published bands. That band is a published South African figure for large, custom or double glazed windows, gathered November 2026. Double glazing roughly doubles the glass cost and needs a system rated to carry the sealed unit, so it is not a glass swap into existing frames. We will tell you honestly when the payback case is weak.

In Tembisa, with housing that is mostly township houses, RDP homes and a growing number of bonded houses, the seasonal pattern is predictable enough to plan around. Booking inside the window costs less than booking in the rush, every year.

What to sort out before the season turns:

- Check whether the opening is measured on site before ordering
- Confirm the frame system name and its powder-coat warranty
- Ask which SANS glass class is being supplied and why

title: Parkhurst pricing: Pressure and Booster Pumps, Pump, pressure vessel and installation quoted as separate lines
long:
If you are pricing Pressure and Booster Pumps in Parkhurst, the number you want is Pump, pressure vessel and installation quoted as separate lines. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: Quoted in three lines so you can see each. The item most often left out of a cheap quote is the pressure vessel, and leaving it out is what causes a booster pump to switch on and off constantly, which destroys it. A quote without a correctly sized vessel is not a cheaper quote, it is a shorter-lived one.

It is quoted per installation, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Parkhurst specifics. A leafy northern Johannesburg suburb of older freestanding houses and cottages, with a main street of shops and restaurants. Housing here is mostly older freestanding houses, cottages and apartments, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: Getting usable pressure out of a tank that is sitting on the ground.

Where quotes go wrong

- No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit
- A pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house
- Drilling before a geohydrological siting report, then paying for a dry hole

What to confirm before you pay anything

- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration
- Confirm the stand's rated load against the full tank weight
- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry

title: The expensive mistake people make with Essential Circuit Wiring
long:
We get called out to the same Essential Circuit Wiring problems over and over in Randfontein. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. No surge protection on the main, then a R40,000 appliance claim
2. Adding solar to a DB board that was already at capacity
3. Buying a CoC without an inspection, which is worthless at claim time

Each one of those turns a job of Priced per board split — the number of circuits moved drives the cost into a bigger one. This is often the cheapest way to make a backup system work better, and it is routinely skipped. Splitting the board so backup feeds only what matters usually lets you buy a smaller inverter or generator, which saves more than the board work costs. We will show you that arithmetic before you buy equipment.

Repairing the crack without fixing the cause just buys you a year.

A live crack filled without addressing the cause reopens within a season, and repeat filling is how people spend more than the proper repair would have cost.

title: "How much is Sand Filter Media Change in Northriding?" — a straight answer
long:
Short answer: Media plus labour, quoted per filter size.

Long answer, because the short one hides the part that matters. The job is priced per filter. Priced on filter size, because that decides how much media goes in and how long the strip-down takes. Filter sand does not last forever — it rounds off, channels and clogs with oils, and then the filter physically cannot remove fine particles no matter how perfect the chemistry is.

Dead filter sand is why your pool will not clear, and almost nobody checks it.

In Northriding specifically, the housing is mostly townhouse complexes, security estates and newer freestanding homes, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

The follow-up questions worth asking:

- Ask how the plan price was derived from your pool's volume
- Confirm whether chemicals are included or billed separately
- Get the pump model and its rated flow against your filter

And the things that push a quote up unexpectedly: a pump sized for the pipework someone else installed; chasing chlorine when the real problem is pH and stabiliser.

title: We fix this Pressure and Booster Pumps mistake every single week
long:
We get called out to the same Pressure and Booster Pumps problems over and over in Constantia Park. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Treating borehole water for taste and ignoring the actual lab test
2. No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit
3. A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper

Each one of those turns a job of Pump, pressure vessel and installation quoted as separate lines into a bigger one. Quoted in three lines so you can see each. The item most often left out of a cheap quote is the pressure vessel, and leaving it out is what causes a booster pump to switch on and off constantly, which destroys it. A quote without a correctly sized vessel is not a cheaper quote, it is a shorter-lived one.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded

title: What goes wrong with Roofing Materials in Vereeniging, and what it costs
long:
We get called out to the same Roofing Materials problems over and over in Vereeniging. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Ordering cement by the bag count instead of by the mix ratio
2. Sand bought by the load with no idea of the cubic metres delivered
3. Storing cement on a slab with no cover through a storm week

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted per square metre of roof area by covering type into a bigger one. Quoted per square metre of roof area. The items left out of cheap roofing quotes are consistent: underlay, ridges, valleys, flashings and fixings. Those are not accessories — the underlay and the flashings are what actually keep highveld driving rain out, and a quote without them is incomplete.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

long:

title: We fix this Iron and Manganese Removal mistake every single week
long:
We get called out to the same Iron and Manganese Removal problems over and over in Lynnwood. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. A pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house
2. A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper
3. Treating borehole water for taste and ignoring the actual lab test

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted on the measured concentration and your flow rate into a bigger one. Quoted from the laboratory figure. Concentration decides the technology: low levels respond to simple filtration media, higher levels need oxidation before filtration, and very high levels need aeration and settling. Fitting a cartridge filter to water with serious iron just means changing a clogged brown cartridge every fortnight.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded

title: Borehole Drilling in Akasia: the price band, before anyone visits
long:
If you are pricing Borehole Drilling in Akasia, the number you want is R350 – R750 per metre on Gauteng drilling-company guides, with other sources claiming R700 – R1,400. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: Four public sources gathered in November 2026 disagree by roughly double on the same job. A drilling-company city guide puts Roodepoort at R350–R650 and Centurion at R420–R750 per metre. A separate cost guide says R700–R1,200 with R950 typical. A June 2026 company announcement cites R900–R1,400. An industry body figure quoted in the press puts the average near R600. None of these is our rate card. The spread exists because sellers quote high, guides quote wide, and nobody states what is included — so ask every quote what the metre rate covers.

It is quoted per metre, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Akasia specifics. A largely suburban area north of the Pretoria CBD with freestanding family homes, security complexes and some smallholdings. Open veld and gardens bring a steady dust load, and light industrial and commercial strips run along the main roads. Housing here is mostly mixed freestanding houses, townhouse complexes and smallholdings, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: What a borehole costs per metre, and why four sources disagree by double.

Where quotes go wrong

- Drilling before a geohydrological siting report, then paying for a dry hole
- A tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper
- No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit

What to confirm before you pay anything

- Confirm the stand's rated load against the full tank weight
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration

title: Budgeting Water Tank Supply and Installation in Heidelberg? Start here
long:
If you are pricing Water Tank Supply and Installation in Heidelberg, the number you want is Tank from about R6,500 for 5,000 L retail; installed line items are quoted at R20,000 – R25,000. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: This is the most useful number on the site. Published retail prices put a 5,000 litre vertical tank at about R6,499 and a 10,000 litre at about R15,599, gathered from a South African source. Yet a storage tank appears on project quotes at R20,000 – R25,000. Both are real. The difference is the base, the stand, the plumbing in and out, the float or level control, the overflow and the labour. We quote the tank and the installation as separate lines so you can see which you are paying for, and so you can compare our tank price with a retailer's directly.

It is quoted per tank | per installation, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Heidelberg specifics. A small town in the Sedibeng area with older freestanding homes and surrounding smallholdings and farmland. Housing here is mostly older freestanding houses and smallholdings, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: Why a R6,500 tank appears as R20,000 on a quote.

Where quotes go wrong

- A pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house
- No first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit
- Treating borehole water for taste and ignoring the actual lab test

What to confirm before you pay anything

- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Confirm the stand's rated load against the full tank weight
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration

Most failed windows need hardware, not replacement.

Priced per repair. We lead with this service deliberately: a very large share of the windows people are told need replacing need rollers, stays, handles or gaskets. What a straight quote from anyone should include:

Before pulling the pump, find out whether the pump is the problem.

Pulling a submersible pump is labour and equipment, and it is worth avoiding when the fault is at the surface. Insulation and continuity tests from the control box identify a failed motor, a damaged cable or a control fault without lifting anything. We do that first and quote the pull separately.

priceBand: R180 – R550 per m³ across published sources, with plaster sand listed at about R439.95 and building sand at about R599 per ton
title: What goes wrong with Sand, Stone and Aggregate in Morningside, and what it costs
long:
We get called out to the same Sand, Stone and Aggregate problems over and over in Morningside. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Ordering cement by the bag count instead of by the mix ratio
2. Sand bought by the load with no idea of the cubic metres delivered
3. Storing cement on a slab with no cover through a storm week

Each one of those turns a job of R180 – R550 per m³ across published sources, with plaster sand listed at about R439.95 and building sand at about R599 per ton into a bigger one. This is the widest disagreement on the whole network. One Gauteng source gives sand at R180 to R220 per cubic metre, another gives R350 to R550, a retailer lists plaster sand at R439.95 per cubic metre and a price guide lists building sand at R599 per ton and builders mix at R425 per cubic metre. Some of those are undated. Sand is also sold by load volume — 10 or 12 cubic metres — with pricing depending on distance from the quarry, which is why no single figure can be right.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Confirm cubic metres on sand and stone, in writing
- Get the quantity schedule, not just a price per unit
- Ask about the returns policy on unopened stock

long:
Short answer: R180 – R550 per m³ across published sources, with plaster sand listed at about R439.95 and building sand at about R599 per ton.

Long answer, because the short one hides the part that matters. The job is priced per m³ | per ton | per load. This is the widest disagreement on the whole network. One Gauteng source gives sand at R180 to R220 per cubic metre, another gives R350 to R550, a retailer lists plaster sand at R439.95 per cubic metre and a price guide lists building sand at R599 per ton and builders mix at R425 per cubic metre. Some of those are undated. Sand is also sold by load volume — 10 or 12 cubic metres — with pricing depending on distance from the quarry, which is why no single figure can be right.

Sand and stone, where published prices differ by three times.

In Centurion specifically, the housing is mostly townhouse estates, freestanding houses and apartments, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

The follow-up questions worth asking:

- Get the quantity schedule, not just a price per unit
- Ask about the returns policy on unopened stock
- Check the cement strength class against the job
- Ask what the delivery fee is per drop and per extra drop

And the things that push a quote up unexpectedly: mixing brick batches mid-wall so the colour steps; ordering cement by the bag count instead of by the mix ratio.

Yet a storage tank appears on project quotes at R20,000 – R25,000. Both are real. The difference is the base, the stand, the plumbing in and out, the float or level control, the overflow and the labour. We quote the tank and the installation as separate lines so you can see which you are paying for, and so you can compare our tank price with a retailer's directly.

We get called out to the same Generator to Inverter Changeover problems over and over in Houghton Estate. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Mounting on a roof that needed sheeting work first
2. A hybrid inverter wired without a proper changeover, so the geyser still trips it
3. Buying panel wattage before sizing the inverter to the actual load

Each one of those turns a job of R12,000 to R25,000 into a bigger one. stop buying petrol at 2am

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Ask for the system's kWh-per-day estimate in writing
- Confirm who carries the roof-penetration waterproofing guarantee
- Ask whether a CoC is issued and who signs it

title: "How much is Inverter and Battery Installation in Midstream Estate?" — a straight answer
long:
Short answer: Electrical installation quoted separately from equipment — essential-circuit scope decides it.

Long answer, because the short one hides the part that matters. The job is priced per installation. We separate the electrical installation from the equipment on every quote, because bundling them is how buyers end up unable to compare anything. The installation cost depends on how many circuits you want backed up, whether the board can be split without rewiring, and where the equipment is mounted relative to the board. We will tell you honestly when a smaller system covering fewer circuits is the better buy.

Backup power wired so it is legal, safe and actually covers what you need.

In Midstream Estate specifically, the housing is mostly estate homes and townhouses, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

The follow-up questions worth asking:

- Ask for the electrician's registration number and check it
- Get the DB board schedule drawn and labelled
- Ask what the earth leakage test actually measured
- Confirm whether remedial work is quoted before or after the inspection

And the things that push a quote up unexpectedly: earth leakage tripping treated as a nuisance instead of a fault; an extension wired in without updating the CoC on record.

long:
It is peak heat and afternoon thunderstorms in Gauteng. That is not small talk — it changes both the price and the queue for Skylights and Roof Glazing.

The band right now is Quoted per unit on size, roof type and flashing detail. Quoted per unit. The product is rarely the problem with skylights — the flashing into the roof covering is. A skylight installed without proper upstands and flashings leaks in the first serious highveld storm, and the leak is usually blamed on the skylight rather than the installation.

In Morningside, with housing that is mostly apartment blocks, townhouses and freestanding houses, the seasonal pattern is predictable enough to plan around. Booking inside the window costs less than booking in the rush, every year.

What to sort out before the season turns:

- Check whether the opening is measured on site before ordering
- Confirm the frame system name and its powder-coat warranty
- Ask which SANS glass class is being supplied and why
- Get the glass thickness and whether it is toughened or laminated

What not to do: clear float glass where SANS requires safety glass; no drainage slots in the sill, so the frame holds water.

title: We fix this Essential Circuit Wiring mistake every single week
long:
We get called out to the same Essential Circuit Wiring problems over and over in Randfontein. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Adding solar to a DB board that was already at capacity
2. Buying a CoC without an inspection, which is worthless at claim time
3. Earth leakage tripping treated as a nuisance instead of a fault

Each one of those turns a job of Priced per board split — the number of circuits moved drives the cost into a bigger one. This is often the cheapest way to make a backup system work better, and it is routinely skipped. Splitting the board so backup feeds only what matters usually lets you buy a smaller inverter or generator, which saves more than the board work costs. We will show you that arithmetic before you buy equipment.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Ask for the electrician's registration number and check it
- A CoC must follow a physical inspection, never a drive-by
- Confirm whether remedial work is quoted before or after the inspection

Green Pool Recovery — R1,500 – R2,500 for a typical recovery. Green water is a diagnosis, not a product — and the cause decides the price.

Pool Safety Nets and Barriers — Quoted on measured pool size and barrier type. Child safety around a pool, and what the by-law actually requires.

title: The expensive mistake people make with Foundations and Underpinning
long:
We get called out to the same Foundations and Underpinning problems over and over in Pretoria West. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. No NHBRC or council approval on work that needed it
2. A quote with no bill of quantities, so every change is a variation claim
3. Snag list agreed verbally and never written down

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted per project after geotechnical and structural assessment into a bigger one. Never quoted before investigation, and be wary of anyone who does. Foundation work follows an engineer's design, and that design follows what trial holes and soil assessment actually find. The cost difference between strengthening a corner and underpinning a whole elevation is enormous, and only investigation tells you which you are facing.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- Confirm which drawings and council approvals are included
- Tie payments to completed stages, never to dates
- Agree the retention percentage held until the snag list closes

long:
Short answer: Surface diagnosis first, then an itemised quote for pulling and repair.

Long answer, because the short one hides the part that matters. The job is priced per job. Pulling a submersible pump is labour and equipment, and it is worth avoiding when the fault is at the surface. Insulation and continuity tests from the control box identify a failed motor, a damaged cable or a control fault without lifting anything. We do that first and quote the pull separately.

Before pulling the pump, find out whether the pump is the problem.

In Three Rivers specifically, the housing is mostly freestanding houses, flats and riverside properties, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

The follow-up questions worth asking:

- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration
- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing
- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry

And the things that push a quote up unexpectedly: a tank stand built for a full tank's weight only on paper; a pressure pump sized for the tap, not for the house.

title: Budgeting Distribution Board Upgrade in Brooklyn? Start here
long:
If you are pricing Distribution Board Upgrade in Brooklyn, the number you want is Estimate only — a residential board replacement typically runs into the low thousands of rand. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: No reliable public price band exists for Gauteng board upgrades, so treat this as an estimate and not a quote. Cost is driven by the number of circuits, whether the board is surface or flush mounted, whether the main cable and earthing need attention, and whether the existing circuits are in a condition to be reconnected without rework. We quote after seeing the board.

It is quoted per board, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Brooklyn specifics. An established Pretoria suburb with older freestanding homes, townhouse complexes and apartment buildings, plus a retail and office node around the mall. Housing here is mostly freestanding houses, townhouses and apartment blocks, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: A board that trips at random, or has no earth leakage at all, is the job worth doing first.

Where quotes go wrong

- No surge protection on the main, then a R40,000 appliance claim
- Earth leakage tripping treated as a nuisance instead of a fault
- An extension wired in without updating the CoC on record

What to confirm before you pay anything

- Ask what the earth leakage test actually measured
- Confirm whether remedial work is quoted before or after the inspection
- Ask for the electrician's registration number and check it
- Get the DB board schedule drawn and labelled
- A CoC must follow a physical inspection, never a drive-by

The band right now is R180 – R550 per m³ across published sources, with plaster sand listed at about R439.95 and building sand at about R599 per ton. One Gauteng source gives sand at R180 to R220 per cubic metre, another gives R350 to R550, a retailer lists plaster sand at R439.95 per cubic metre and a price guide lists building sand at R599 per ton and builders mix at R425 per cubic metre. Some of those are undated. Sand is also sold by load volume — 10 or 12 cubic metres — with pricing depending on distance from the quarry, which is why no single figure can be right.

In Wierda Park, with housing that is mostly freestanding houses and townhouse complexes, the seasonal pattern is predictable enough to plan around. Booking inside the window costs less than booking in the rush, every year.

What to sort out before the season turns:

- Ask about the returns policy on unopened stock
- Check the cement strength class against the job
- Ask what the delivery fee is per drop and per extra drop

What not to do: sand bought by the load with no idea of the cubic metres delivered; no wastage allowance, then a second delivery fee for 40 bricks.

Approval runs through your municipality, and they all work differently.

Drawings and submission are quoted per project; municipal fees are the council's and are paid to them directly. - Tie payments to completed stages, never to dates

- Agree the retention percentage held until the snag list closes

long:

Measuring what your installation actually draws, before you guess at an upgrade.

A survey is priced on how many boards are involved and how long we log for. Logging over a working week costs more than a spot reading and is worth it when the question is whether to pay for a supply upgrade, because that decision is usually worth far more than the survey.

Why the price is published. Most trades in Gauteng quote only after a site visit, which makes comparing three quotes a week-long job. We publish the band first so you can decide whether the project is worth starting before anyone books your Saturday.

- Agree the retention percentage held until the snag list closes

title: Choosing between Stove and Oven Connection and Distribution Board Upgrade
long:
Two ways to spend money on the same problem in Nigel, and they are not interchangeable.

Stove and Oven Connection — Priced per appliance — connection on an existing circuit costs far less than a new one. Hobs, ovens and stoves need their own circuit — not the kitchen plug ring.

Distribution Board Upgrade — Estimate only — a residential board replacement typically runs into the low thousands of rand. A board that trips at random, or has no earth leakage at all, is the job worth doing first.

When the first one wins: when the scope is clear, the property is standard for Nigel, and you want the smaller number to actually hold.

When the second one wins: when the first option would need to be redone inside two years, which is the only comparison that matters.

Either way, confirm these before you choose:

- A CoC must follow a physical inspection, never a drive-by

Each one of those turns a job of Priced as a detection visit, with repair quoted once located into a bigger one. Detection and repair are separate because they are separate jobs. long:
We get called out to the same Electric Fence Certificate of Compliance problems over and over in Rosebank. They are not exotic. They are cheap to avoid and expensive to fix.

1. Buying a CoC without an inspection, which is worthless at claim time
2. Adding solar to a DB board that was already at capacity
3. Earth leakage tripping treated as a nuisance instead of a fault

Each one of those turns a job of Quoted after a look at the fence — length, energiser and warning signage decide it into a bigger one. No reliable public price band exists for Gauteng electric fence certification, so we do not publish one. The cost is driven by the perimeter length, the number of zones, the age and type of the energiser, and how much of the existing installation has to be corrected. We quote after seeing the fence, and the inspection and the repairs are always separate lines.

The fix is boring: ask for the scope in writing, ask what the price is based on, and ask who carries the guarantee.

- A CoC must follow a physical inspection, never a drive-by
- Ask for the electrician's registration number and check it
- Get the DB board schedule drawn and labelled

Sand and stone, where published prices differ by three times.

This is the widest disagreement on the whole network. One Gauteng source gives sand at R180 to R220 per cubic metre, another gives R350 to R550, a retailer lists plaster sand at R439.95 per cubic metre and a price guide lists building sand at R599 per ton and builders mix at R425 per cubic metre. - Get the quantity schedule, not just a price per unit

title: Hardware and Fixings in Lynnwood — published prices, free quote
long:
Hardware and Fixings in Lynnwood: Quoted per box or per unit.

Fixings matched to what they are going into.

Frameless Shower Doors in Moreleta Park runs Quoted per enclosure on glass size, configuration and hardware. Most of the money people lose on it is not lost on the price — it is lost in what nobody agreed before the work started.

Five things to confirm, in writing, first:

1. Get the glass thickness and whether it is toughened or laminated
2. Ask which SANS glass class is being supplied and why
3. Confirm the frame system name and its powder-coat warranty
4. Check whether the opening is measured on site before ordering
5. Ask whether removal, making good and sealing are included

Context on the pricing: Quoted per enclosure after measuring the finished tiled opening. Frameless glass has no frame to absorb an out-of-square wall, which is why we measure after tiling rather than before. Ordering from a builder's drawing is the most common reason a frameless shower does not fit.

Moreleta Park is mostly townhouse complexes and freestanding houses. Ask how your specific property changes the band — a good contractor can answer that in one sentence.

title: Johannesburg South, late summer storms and hail risk: the Essential Circuit Wiring window is open
long:
It is late summer storms and hail risk in Gauteng. That is not small talk — it changes both the price and the queue for Essential Circuit Wiring.

The band right now is Priced per board split — the number of circuits moved drives the cost. This is often the cheapest way to make a backup system work better, and it is routinely skipped. Splitting the board so backup feeds only what matters usually lets you buy a smaller inverter or generator, which saves more than the board work costs. We will show you that arithmetic before you buy equipment.

In Johannesburg South, with housing that is mostly older freestanding houses, townhouses and some light industry, the seasonal pattern is predictable enough to plan around. Booking inside the window costs less than booking in the rush, every year.

What to sort out before the season turns:

- Ask for the electrician's registration number and check it
- Get the DB board schedule drawn and labelled
- Confirm whether remedial work is quoted before or after the inspection
- A CoC must follow a physical inspection, never a drive-by

What not to do: no surge protection on the main, then a R40,000 appliance claim; earth leakage tripping treated as a nuisance instead of a fault.

title: "How much is Borehole Drilling in Meyerton?" — a straight answer
long:
Short answer: R350 – R750 per metre on Gauteng drilling-company guides, with other sources claiming R700 – R1,400.

A drilling-company city guide puts Roodepoort at R350–R650 and Centurion at R420–R750 per metre. A separate cost guide says R700–R1,200 with R950 typical. A June 2026 company announcement cites R900–R1,400. An industry body figure quoted in the press puts the average near R600. None of these is our rate card. The spread exists because sellers quote high, guides quote wide, and nobody states what is included — so ask every quote what the metre rate covers.

What a borehole costs per metre, and why four sources disagree by double.

In Meyerton specifically, the housing is mostly freestanding houses, golf estates and smallholdings, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing

title: Beaulieu: your Payment Schedules and Retention questions, answered without a sales call
long:
Short answer: Included in project management, or priced as a standalone advisory piece.

Long answer, because the short one hides the part that matters. The job is priced per project. Available as part of project management or on its own. The single most common way homeowners lose money on a build is paying ahead of the work — a builder who is paid sixty per cent for forty per cent of progress has no commercial reason to finish, and every reason to start someone else's job.

Paying against measured progress, not against the builder's cash flow.

In Beaulieu specifically, the housing is mostly estates, smallholdings and freestanding houses, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

The follow-up questions worth asking:

- Tie payments to completed stages, never to dates
- Ask for the programme with weather days shown
- Insist on a bill of quantities with the quote
- Confirm which drawings and council approvals are included

And the things that push a quote up unexpectedly: a quote with no bill of quantities, so every change is a variation claim; snag list agreed verbally and never written down.

title: Green Pool Recovery in Greenstone Hill: the price band, before anyone visits
long:
If you are pricing Green Pool Recovery in Greenstone Hill, the number you want is R1,500 – R2,500 for a typical recovery. That is a band, not a promise — but it is a real band, published up front, and it is close enough to budget against.

How that number is derived: Band published by a Johannesburg operator and gathered November 2026 — indicative, not our rate card. Recovery times of 24 to 72 hours are commonly advertised and are realistic for a chemical recovery on sound equipment. What changes the price is the cause. A pool that went green because nobody dosed it recovers on chemicals. A pool that went green because the filter media is dead, the pump is not circulating, or the stabiliser is so high that chlorine cannot work needs that fixed first, and no amount of shock treatment substitutes.

It is quoted per job, which matters: two quotes on different bases are not comparable, however similar the rand figure looks.

Greenstone Hill specifics. An Edenvale-area suburb with a large retail and office node and a mix of townhouse complexes, apartments and freestanding houses. Housing here is mostly townhouse complexes, apartments and freestanding houses, and that drives the final figure more than anything a call centre will tell you.

What we are actually talking about: Green water is a diagnosis, not a product — and the cause decides the price.

Where quotes go wrong

- A pump sized for the pipework someone else installed
- Topping up a leak for a year instead of pressure-testing the lines
- A weekly plan priced by phone call instead of by actual pool volume

What to confirm before you pay anything

- Check what the visit actually covers, task by task
- Ask for a pressure test before any leak quote
- Get the pump model and its rated flow against your filter
- Confirm whether chemicals are included or billed separately
- Ask how the plan price was derived from your pool's volume

title: The question we get asked most about Water Filtration Systems
long:
Short answer: Quoted per system once the water analysis is in hand.

Long answer, because the short one hides the part that matters. The job is priced per installation. We will not quote filtration before seeing a water analysis, and we would be suspicious of anyone who does. The correct system depends entirely on what is in the water — and on flow rate, which is the variable most often ignored until the pressure drops through an undersized filter.

Filtration specified from a laboratory result, not from a brochure.

In Moreleta Park specifically, the housing is mostly townhouse complexes and freestanding houses, so the band tends to sit where you would expect rather than at either extreme.

The follow-up questions worth asking:

- Get the yield in litres per hour, tested and recorded
- Ask for a water lab analysis before buying any filtration
- Check whether the pump warranty survives running dry
- Ask for the siting report and the dry-hole policy in writing

And the things that push a quote up unexpectedly: treating borehole water for taste and ignoring the actual lab test; no first-flush diverter on a harvesting setup, so the tank collects roof grit.
